claim: At player-start the game spawns COLR as a STANDING process (life-scoped, not per-entity) — the laser colour cycler runs for the whole life.
At player-start the game spawns CBOMB as a STANDING process — the bomb colour cycler (registers A and C) runs for the whole life.
At player-start the game spawns TIECOL as a STANDING process — the TIE colour cycler (registers D/E/F) runs for the whole life.
The frame IRQ copies the 16-byte PCRAM shadow into hardware CRAM every frame (the *COLOR MAPPING block), so a mutated shadow re-colours the screen next frame.
COLR stores each COLTAB entry into PCRAM+1 (the LASER register, palette index 1).
COLR sleeps 2 ticks between laser colour steps (LDA #2 before JMP SLEEP).
COLR wraps the laser colour walk at the COLTAB $00 terminator (BEQ COLR resets the index).
COLTAB (laser/bomb colour table) bytes 0-4 are $38,$39,$3A,$3B,$3C.
COLTAB bytes 19-26 are $C6,$C5,$CC,$CB,$CA,$DA,$E8,$F8.
COLTAB bytes 27-34 are $F9,$FA,$FB,$FD,$FF,$BF,$3F,$3E.
COLTAB byte 35 is $3C, followed by the 0 terminator that wraps the COLR walk.
CBOMB writes the $FF flash into PCRAM+$A (bomb register A, palette index 10).
CBOMB blacks PCRAM+$C on the flash phase (bomb register C, palette index 12 — the mutant index-12 pixel).
On the colour phase CBOMB writes the picked COLTAB colour into PCRAM+$C.
TIECOL stores a TCTAB row's first two bytes into PCRAM+$D/$E (TIE registers D and E).
TIECOL stores a TCTAB row's third byte into PCRAM+$F (TIE register F).
TCTAB (TIE colour table) row 0 is $81,$81,$2F.
TCTAB row 1 is $81,$2F,$07.
TCTAB row 2 is $2F,$81,$07.
